summary: Spanish-built 1893 light on Point Figuras at Arroyo, Puerto Rico; moved and boarded up in 1938, damaged by vandals, on the National Register since 1981; not open to enter.

structures.type: octagonal tower rising from the middle of a flat-roofed dwelling
structures.note: The 1981 nomination describes ruins; a travel account says the building was rehabilitated in 2002-03 and boarded up again after 2017.

access.note: Sources disagree. LighthouseFriends: owned by the Puerto Rico Department of Natural Resources; 'Grounds/tower open'; reportedly open daily 9 a.m. to 3 p.m. US Lighthouse Society archive: Open to Public: No. Travel account (undated): not in use nor open to enter, outside can be walked around. NRHP nomination (1981): 'Unrestricted access', out of date.

corrections.why: The NRHP nomination, LighthouseFriends, the Arroyo municipal page and EnciclopediaPR give construction in 1892-1893 and first lighting in 1893. The 1889 date comes from the USLHS record, which the nomination and the Spanish sources contradict. The 1901 Light-House Board report does not give an earlier date for the light.
The nomination dates the original Barbier, Benard & Cie lens to 1892 (lenticular, 37.5 cm diameter), not 1889.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The USLHS place record gives Guayama as town and county. The NRHP nomination, the Arroyo municipal page and EnciclopediaPR place the light in Arroyo, which the station record keeps.
USLHS: 1889. Nomination, Spanish sources and LighthouseFriends: construction 1892-1893, lit 1893. The 1889 event is kept in the record's events but flagged in corrections.

notes_for_editor: Punta de las Figuras, fact-check of 2026-10-27. All 49 original evidence quotes were found in their cached sources on the first run. Corrections made: (1) the story said no source names the present owner; LighthouseFriends names the Puerto Rico Department of Natural Resources and says grounds and tower are open, and gives opening hours; the Today section now states that the sources disagree, and the JSON access level is 'unknown' with the conflict recorded; (2) the 1906 notice is dated by its Spanish text to 8 November 1906 for the change of colours, not as the notice's own date; the story now says the notice was printed 9 November; (3) 'Our translation' changed to 'Translated from the Spanish' (first person); (4) the 1901 Light-House Board volume is the fiscal year ended 30 June 1901 (corpus heading); (5) the 'Domingo Suarez' link: the story now rests on the 1924-1929 index itself, which lists Domingo Suarez as keeper of the six stations the 1925 notice names and also has an entry 'Rosa, Domingo Suarez, retired keeper, dead'; the earlier station-match reasoning is retired; (6) 'along the coast' and 'a difficult site' removed as unsourced; (7) 'the island's eastern end' changed to 'eastern Puerto Rico' as the NRHP says; (8) the efficiency-flag rule is attributed to LighthouseFriends' quotation of the regulation; (9) footnotes added to unfootnoted sentences (lead, Spanish kitchen, 1938, reopened, Army lease). Matched by position or OCR: 'Castro, Loenzo' in the 1918-1923 index is matched by station to Lorenzo Castro-Gonzales (USLHS roster, LighthouseFriends; the 1920-1922 Bulletin keeper lists also read 'Lorenzo Castro' at Point Figuras). The index page image was not read; the OCR of that entry was checked against the corpus text, and the station and keeper are corroborated by USLHS and LighthouseFriends. The 1925 notice OCR reads 'Guaniea' for Guanica and 'Sufirez' for Suarez; the story uses the index spelling. The NRHP 'listed since 1981' rests on the form's stamp 'OCT.-22:1981' (OCR) and the 81- reference number; the second page's date stamps are garbled, so the exact listing date was not confirmed from the NPGallery record. The 1906 English notice OCR reads 'green window Bhuttsrs'; the green shutters are supported by the Spanish 'persianas de verde' and the English reading in context. HAER PR-39 (loc.gov) was not read (403). Wikipedia not used. Current owner per LighthouseFriends is a 1990s-2000s statement; no other source read names the owner. The USLHS record gives Guayama as city and county; the story keeps Arroyo as the NRHP, Arroyo municipal page and EnciclopediaPR do.
